recordings.transcript: So I would split it into an ingestion pipeline and a query pipeline. On ingestion I chunk along the document structure, headings and sections, so a fact does not get cut in half. At query time I run both keyword search and vector search, because product names match lexically but paraphrased questions need embeddings. Then a reranker takes the top fifty down to maybe eight chunks before the model sees them. I would log ingestion and querying separately too. If answers were wrong I would look at the prompt first and then try a bigger model.

sentences.text: So I would split it into an ingestion pipeline and a query pipeline.
On ingestion I chunk along the document structure, headings and sections, so a fact does not get cut in half.
At query time I run both keyword search and vector search, because product names match lexically but paraphrased questions need embeddings.
The user's permissions go into that search query as a filter, so a chunk they are not allowed to see is never retrieved at all.
sentences.rubricLine: Access is enforced in the retrieval query so a caller never receives a chunk they are not allowed to see

sentences.text: Then a reranker takes the top fifty down to maybe eight chunks before the model sees them.
I would log ingestion and querying separately too.
If answers were wrong I would first score retrieval on its own, with questions labelled with the chunk they need, because one end-to-end score would not tell me whether search or generation failed.

sentences.text: Our search is basically perfect so this rarely matters.

recordings.transcript: First I would check whether the right clause was even in the retrieved chunks. I would measure retrieval separately from generation, with a set of contract questions and the clause each one needs, because one end to end score would not tell me which half broke. If the clause was retrieved and the answer is still wrong, that is a generation problem, maybe the clause sat at the end of a long context. When search returns nothing relevant the model should say it does not know instead of answering from memory. Every answer would cite the chunk it came from.
